target_customer: Sales organizations (managers, sales ops, finance) that pay sales commissions
problem: Commissions are the biggest strategic lever and a large expense for sales teams, yet they are administered in Excel and email, so reps cannot see how they are pacing and disputes are hard to trace (YC page).
business_model: B2B SaaS for sales commission tracking (pricing not found)

competitors.name: Xactly
competitors.what: Cloud sales compensation and incentive management for revenue operations executives
competitors.traction_then: $64M sales in 12 months to 2015-04-30; IPO planned June 2015 on NYSE

technical_complexity.rationale: Calculation engine plus CRM and payroll data integrations; commission plans are complex to model but standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Plan history and payout data create some stickiness, but the product was copyable and a public incumbent existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents ignored a tiny YC wedge; the segment later consolidated (Xactly taken private by Vista in 2017, Spiff bought by Salesforce), but nothing links this to Compgun.

market_need_then: YC page states commissions run on Excel and email; no dated external evidence of spend or complaints found. A public Xactly with $64M sales in 2015 shows paying demand for commission software.

branding.domain_note: compgun.com did not resolve in November 2026 (DNS failure).

brand_strength.rationale: Nothing found beyond the YC page and aggregators; the gun metaphor sits oddly with a finance tool but no source says it mattered.

outcome_analysis: YC lists Compgun as inactive and CB Insights says it ceased operations, but no founder post-mortem, news story or shutdown notice was found, so the cause and date of closure are not public. Only a small seed-sized amount is reported by aggregators and the company never appears in press, so the record cannot say whether it failed on demand, competition, funding or founder choice. The founder later started Aero.com per YC.
notes: Unverified aggregator figure: CB Insights and Bouncewatch both list a $120K round from Y Combinator dated 2016-03-22/23; this matches YC's standard deal so it is not recorded as a round. CB Insights says 'ceased operations' (aggregator only). A 'Acquired' label on a CB Insights compare page belongs to Spiff, not Compgun. Callidus was Xactly's main rival per 451 Research (undated post-IPO); not listed as I lack a source dated near 2016. Searches for 2016-dated competitor coverage returned only 2024 to 2026 vendor blogs. Branding search found nothing on name origin.
